section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 1: AWS AI Monetization vs. CapEx Return on Invested Capital (ROIC)
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls argue that AWS's multi-billion dollar investment in custom Trainium2 chips, Bedrock enterprise model hubs, and Nvidia Blackwell clusters is already driving re-accelerating revenue growth past +22% YoY with industry-leading 38%+ cloud operating margins. Bears contend that $44B+ in quarterly CapEx ($100B+ run-rate) has pushed quarterly reported Free Cash Flow into negative territory (-$18.2B in Q2 2026), creating an overhang if cloud clients optimize spend or GenAI inference software commoditizes.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: Can Andy Jassy provide quantitative proof that enterprise generative AI revenue is scaling at triple-digit rates, and when will annual CapEx intensity plateau relative to operating cash flows?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 2: Retail Margin Durability & Regionalized Fulfillment Cost Reductions
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls emphasize that Amazon's regionalized fulfillment network, automated robotics (Sequoia, Proteus), and higher delivery densities have permanently lowered the cost-to-serve per unit while accelerating same-day and one-day delivery speeds. Bears warn that discount cross-border platforms (Temu, Shein) are forcing Amazon to lower 3P apparel take rates and introduce low-cost storefronts, while consumers exhibit cautious discretionary basket sizes.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: How much further can North America and International retail operating margins expand, and what impact is the low-cost direct-from-China storefront having on 3P take rates?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 3: Advertising Services Scale & Prime Video Ad-Tier Monetization
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls view Amazon Advertising ($19.8B in Q2, ~80%+ gross margin) as the ultimate high-margin cash engine, scaling rapidly as default Prime Video advertising tiers attract top-tier consumer brand budgets away from linear TV. Bears argue that retail media growth must eventually decelerate towards broader digital advertising GDP rates (+10–12%) and that excessive sponsored listings could degrade the shopper search experience.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: What is the current ad-tier adoption rate across Prime Video subscribers globally, and what incremental operating profit does advertising contribute to retail operations?
